rule: Partners of a property-predominant company not subject to IS enter IRF. For this chapter, more than 50% of company turnover must be article102 property income. A company subject to IS is not brought into the individual IRF computation merely because it owns a building.

rule: Article102 covers built and non-built property income, furnished letting, fixed industrial installations, building-lease rent and property-right ancillary income, only where the income is not included in business profits of an industrial/commercial enterprise, farm or noncommercial profession. rule: The resulting IRF is increased by a separate FCFA4,000 ORTB levy. IRF and this levy appear distinctly on the same collection title as TFU; they are not a single combined percentage.

rule: Tenant withholding is 12% of gross rent, reduced to 10% where the landlord is subject to IBA or IS. The 10% is a withholding classification, not a replacement individual IRF rate for every landlord.

rule: Natural-person tenants are exempt from withholding, except those renting through an entity subject to tax on profits. Do not infer withholding exemption from a natural-person landlord.

rule: Start with gross rent. Add owner expenses contractually borne by the tenant, and subtract tenant expenses the owner paid for the tenant. Keep supporting contracts and invoices; the statute does not give this job a general percentage expense allowance.

rule: Owner-occupied housing has no imputed rental IRF under article102(2). By contrast, free provision to a third person without a legal obligation creates in-kind income valued under article157. The legal-obligation distinction must be evidenced before setting the imputed base to zero.

rule: Prepare separate columns for gross rent paid, the adjusted article103 IRF base, the ORTB levy, withholding actually remitted and instalments. A promise or unsupported deduction is not a paid-and-remitted receipt.

rule: Article106(3) calls withholding final but keeps the annual declaration. Do not infer a general refund or merge the ORTB charge into withholding. rule: By 10 February annually, give the competent tax service a statement naming tenants, prior-year rent received and withholding suffered. rule: Remit withholding spontaneously by the 10th for the preceding month’s rent. If rent was paid in advance, withhold and remit by the 10th of the month following the actual advance payment; do not spread the remittance over the accommodation months.

rule: IRF uses four instalments as for IBA, which article66 pays as IS: provisionally one quarter of preceding-year tax by 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December. If the prior return is not filed by the first instalment, article51 uses the penultimate year provisionally, regularised at the second instalment. Offset supported withholding without duplicating it.
